description: SOC2 Type II compliance framework layer — append-only audit log, change-management approvals (CC8.1), vendor registry, and incident-response playbook. Composes onto any Node/TypeScript backend.

buildHints.whenToUse: Bolt SOC2 Type II primitives (audit trail, change-management approvals, vendor registry) onto an existing Node/TypeScript backend before a Type II audit window opens.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm build` (`tsc --noEmit`) — must pass with zero errors.
Run `node validate-soc2-pack.mjs` to confirm required files and logic are present.
Wire `recordChange()` from `src/change-mgmt.ts` onto every deploy and config change — CC8.1 requires change approvals to be logged.
Replace `InMemorySocAuditStore` with a DB-backed implementation before going to production (audit logs must persist across restarts).
Fill in `docs/vendor-attestations.md` with every sub-processor (Stripe, AWS, Vercel, etc.) and their SOC2 report links.
gotchas: Audit log retention for SOC2 is commonly 12 months minimum; some auditors require 7 years. Confirm before TTL-ing old rows.
Change management (CC8.1) requires ≥1 approver per change — self-merges are flagged. Enforce via branch protection, not honor system.
Vendor attestations must be CURRENT (within the audit window). A 2-year-old vendor SOC2 report is an exception finding.
Incident response (CC7.3) needs a tested playbook. Run at least one tabletop exercise before the audit.
architectureNotes: SOC2 audits are about process evidence, not code. This pack produces the artifacts (audit rows, CODEOWNERS, playbooks) auditors want to see. The controls themselves are operational.
`InMemorySocAuditStore` is intentionally a drop-in; swap it for a Postgres/SQLite implementation by implementing the `SocAuditStore` interface.

placeholders.description: Trust Services Criteria CC1–CC9 mapped to files. Customize the scope section per your actual audit.
Live sub-processor registry. Add every vendor with a SOC2 report and update at least quarterly.
